title: The Last Terminal Revisited
premise: Mara Reyes smuggles forbidden memories between the silent worlds of the Meridian Belt, keeping her head down and her past sealed. When the derelict ship Halcyon returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children who remember their own deaths, orbital authorities seize it—and Mara discovers her own sealed memories are the key to why the Halcyon's reactor is counting down. The countdown will wake only half of the two thousand colonists in cryosleep aboard, and the factions that once split humanity now fight over which half. In the end, Mara sacrifices her contraband identity—wiping her own memories—to broadcast the truth to both worlds, letting the children of the Halcyon choose for themselves as the reactor's final cycle begins.
about_author: Marguerite Almeida is a former radio archivist from Lisbon who writes science fiction about what people choose to remember and what they choose to forget. She lives above a decommissioned tram depot with her partner and an aging cat named Capacitor.

chapters.title: Contraband
chapters.summary: Mara runs a memory shipment through orbital customs at Meridian Station, hiding stolen recollections in her own neural cache. POV: Mara. The beat establishes her loneliness and skill, ending when she learns a ship thought lost forty years has just reappeared at the edge of the Belt.

chapters.title: The Halcyon Returns
chapters.summary: Mara witnesses the Halcyon docking: two thousand cryopods intact, but the crew are children who speak of their own deaths in fluent detail. POV: Mara, with a brief interlude from a child-crewman named Ivo. The emotional beat is uncanny dread—the impossible made bureaucratic.

chapters.title: Sealed
chapters.summary: Customs scans flag Mara's hidden cache; the Halcyon's children react to her presence like she's family. POV: Mara. She realizes her sealed memories connect her to the Halcyon's mission, and the chapter ends with her deciding, against every instinct, not to run.

chapters.title: Two Worlds, No Words
chapters.summary: Flashback chapters within Mara's fractured cache reveal the schism: Meridian and Ceres severed contact after the Halcyon launched, each blaming the other. POV: alternating Mara-present and memory-Mara. The beat is grief—she helped build the silence she now smuggles through.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: The Halcyon's reactor begins an automated wake-cycle: enough power to revive exactly half the colonists before failing permanently. Both governments claim jurisdiction. POV: Ivo, the child-crewman, watching adults become what he died trying to prevent. The beat is rising dread and moral vertigo.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: Meridian offers Mara full amnesty to unlock her cache for them; Ceres offers the same through a back channel. POV: Mara. Torn between factions, she realizes both want to weaponize her memories to justify choosing 'their' half. Emotional beat: betrayal by institutions she never trusted but needed.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Ivo and the other age-reversed crew reveal the truth: the Halcyon found something in deep space that rewinds time around guilt, and it followed them home. POV: Ivo. The beat is wonder curdling into horror—the reactor countdown isn't malfunction; it's the phenomenon, still hungry.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: With hours left, both fleets position to seize the Halcyon by force. Mara unlocks her full cache publicly: she was the mission's comms officer, erased and sent back to keep the secret. POV: Mara. Climactic beat—she chooses neither faction, broadcasting everything to both worlds at once.

chapters.title: Terminal
chapters.summary: In the reactor chamber, Mara offers the phenomenon what it actually wants—not a choice of halves, but a witness: someone to carry the memory of everyone. She wipes herself as the transfer completes. POV: shifting to Ivo holding her empty body's hand. The beat is sacrifice without certainty.

chapters.title: Revisited
chapters.summary: The countdown stops; all pods hold power long enough for a slow, shared awakening over years instead of one brutal triage. A woman wakes on Meridian with no name and a stranger's memories singing in her head. POV: the new Mara. Final beat: belonging rebuilt from loss—two worlds, speaking again.
